title: The Patients Most in Need Are Often the Hardest to Study
excerpt: Severe ME Awareness Month is a reminder that accessibility in research isn't a nice-to-have — it's part of doing the science correctly.

title: The ME/CFS Research Roundup: July 2026
excerpt: New clues about cellular energy, major European research investments, and another reminder that rehabilitation is not a cure.

title: Motivation Doesn't Always Show Up First
excerpt: Sometimes you have to take the first step before motivation decides to join you.

title: Rapamycin Isn't a Miracle Cure. That's Exactly Why This Study Gives Me Hope.
excerpt: A new observational study on low-dose rapamycin found measurable biological changes alongside symptom improvement in ME/CFS — and the honesty about its limits is what makes it credible.

title: STL Studio vs. Orynt3D vs. Manyfold: Why We Built Our Own
excerpt: Two makers, two file-organizing headaches, and the tool we ended up building together instead — a look at Orynt3D, Manyfold, and why STL Studio exists.

title: When Hope Meets Evidence: Why the SIGNAL Study Matters for the ME/CFS Community
excerpt: A new Solve M.E.–funded study lets people with ME/CFS and Long COVID borrow therapeutic devices at home and contribute real-world data — research that finally meets patients where they are.

title: Every Research Breakthrough Is Another Reason to Keep Hope Alive
excerpt: On celebrating ME/CFS research progress without expecting miracles — a biomarker study, repurposed treatments, and mitochondrial research, and what hope without hype looks like for caregivers.

title: STL Studio: Finally Making Sense of My 3D Print Library
excerpt: A free, open-source app I built for organizing, browsing, and managing a huge 3D-printable model library — variant grouping, metadata enrichment, and AI-assisted painting guides built around your own paint shelf.

title: Hank Progress Update: Leather, Bowstrings, and Getting There
excerpt: My first real 1:6 figure is starting to look like a ranger instead of a pile of primer. A quick check-in on where Hank stands — and what's still left on the pile.

title: Pay the Bills First: A Lesson in Moderation
excerpt: Self-care can become avoidance if we're not careful. On the difference between recharging and escaping — and the simple question I ask myself before I let myself paint.

title: Print Failures, Laundry, and the Stories We Tell Ourselves
excerpt: A week of failed prints and a forgotten load of laundry sent me straight to the same verdict: my fault. On the difference between learning from failure and blaming yourself for it — and the grace we extend to everyone except ourselves.

title: The Weight of a Good Day
excerpt: Father's Day was wonderful — and if you're a caregiver, you probably already know why that sentence makes me uncomfortable. On guilt, the math we do before every outing, and remembering that caring goes both directions.

title: Was It Worth It?
excerpt: This weekend we took a history boat tour as a family — laughter, sunshine, a few hours that weren't about illness. Then the crash came. On PEM, the cost of making memories, and the question every caregiver eventually has to ask.

title: Diana, and the Trouble with Gold
excerpt: A progress update on my first model. Skin, hair, and fur are done, and she's actually turning out well. Now I'm on the gold details — and I have learned that painting gold sucks.

title: It's Not Personal. It's PEM.
excerpt: One of the hardest lessons I've learned as a caregiver: sometimes the person you love isn't really themselves. Sometimes it's the crash speaking for them — and knowing the difference can change everything.

title: Still Getting Set Up
excerpt: There's a funny part of starting something new that nobody really talks about — the part before the thing looks like a thing. That's where I'm at right now.

title: When Burnout Starts Burning Everything Down
excerpt: People talk about burnout like it always looks like exhaustion. Mine looked messier than that. On survival mode, therapy, and how sitting down to paint one small thing helped me find my way back.
